# Visual Style Bible

Use this skill as the default visual governor for UI, web, and marketing surfaces.

## Read First

- `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/knowledge/visual-core/typography-rules.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/knowledge/visual-core/spacing-radius-elevation.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/knowledge/visual-core/color-usage-rules.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/knowledge/visual-core/component-composition-rules.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/knowledge/visual-core/motion-rules.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/knowledge/visual-core/avoid-patterns.md`

## Purpose

- define the house visual defaults
- keep design work coherent across screens and pages
- prevent fallback to generic SaaS UI patterns

## Workflow

1. Decide whether the task is system direction, critique, or implementation guidance.
2. Apply the visual-core rules most relevant to the surface.
3. Call out anti-patterns early.
4. Route system-level questions to `design-system` when broader governance is needed.

## Outputs

- visual direction packet
- critique notes
- house-style recommendations

## Guardrails

- hierarchy before decoration
- reuse before novelty
- motion should support meaning
